clue.text: Badger bringing pestilence

definitions.meaning: to badger someone is to pester or harass them persistently
a deadly epidemic disease, such as the bubonic outbreaks of history

explanation.surface: A badger is blamed for spreading disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the verb means to pester relentlessly, and the noun is a deadly epidemic.

clue.text: Write on runaway classic weaver

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to pen is to write
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: A writer takes up the story of a classic weaver who fled.
explanation.walkthrough: PENELOPE, wife of Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey, wove a shroud by day and unpicked it by night to delay her suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithful wife in Homer's epic famously weaves and unweaves a shroud, so she is the classical weaver.

clue.text: One who checks cost getting first class return on large halls

parts.note: an auditor checks a company's accounts and spending

indicators.note: return says the letters for first class are turned round

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An accountant secures top-rated return on big venues.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a standard way of saying first class, and crosswords read the digit 1 as the letter I; 'on' places the turned pair below in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is a plural of auditorium, a large hall where an audience gathers.

clue.text: Fruit can be unattractive, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that a word spoken aloud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: ugly means unattractive

explanation.surface: Some fruit can look rather unappealing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with a lumpy skin.

clue.text: Main picture of second flight across America

indicators.note: across says one piece spans another, holding it inside

parts.note: a flight is an escape, as in fleeing

explanation.surface: A painting of a second flight across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not 'principal'. 'across' puts A inside ESCAPE as E-A-SCAPE, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture of the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean.

clue.text: Waste away? But I came up and had a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone protests they cannot be wasting away, having just eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads I CAME from the bottom in this down clue; the question mark flags that the definition is a query rather than a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to become abnormally thin, wasting away through lack of food.

clue.text: Counterfeit first edition? Looked straight at it, humiliated

parts.note: a sham is a counterfeit or fake

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to face something is to look directly at it

explanation.surface: Someone confronted with a forged first edition is embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced describes someone showing embarrassment or shame, as when humiliated.

clue.text: Concur that daughter has abandoned a vice

indicators.note: has abandoned says a letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins, a vice
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Agreement that a daughter has given up a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to concur, being of the same opinion.

clue.text: Middle East involved in tiny shake-up producing animosity

indicators.note: involved in says the two pieces are mixed up together before the jumble
a shake-up rearranges, signalling the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A minor upheaval in the Middle East breeds hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' and 'shake-up' together say the two-letter abbreviation is churned in with tiny as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or ill will, a synonym of animosity.

clue.text: Show the way user swallows heroin

indicators.note: swallows means the word takes another inside it

parts.note: H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user taking heroin leads the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to guide or show them the way, as an usher does.

clue.text: Lumps of drug unsold? Strange

indicators.note: Strange signals that the letters are reworked into an odd new order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer wonders why lumps of a drug remain unsold.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodules are small rounded lumps, as in the body or in rock.

clue.text: It can make much of chum

definitions.text: It can make much of chum

parts.words: It can make much of chum
parts.note: the letters of chum rearranged spell much, so the thing that does this is a wordplay device, not a fond friend

explanation.surface: Something that can flatter a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one word to make another, such as chum to much, is this wordplay device.

clue.text: Heaps of things for sale

definitions.meaning: items offered at auction are numbered as separate units

explanation.surface: Plenty of goods on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a great many; at auction each item offered is one of these.

clue.text: Frisky terrier lost tail, started tagging after people leaving work

indicators.note: after places the letter behind the people
frisky suggests lively movement, so these letters are jumbled
lost tail drops the final letter of the dog

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: started takes the beginning letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A lively dog that lost its tail began following people as they quit work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost tail' drops the last R of terrier and 'Frisky' mixes the remaining six letters; 'started' takes only the first letter of tagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is the act of leaving one's working life for good.

clue.text: Tables of figures can make one sit up in stable society

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other

parts.note: static means stable or unchanging

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Statistics can startle anyone in steady society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads SIT bottom to top in this down clue; 'can make one' merely links, echoing the idiom 'make one sit up', meaning to startle.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistics are numerical data, typically set out in tables of figures.

clue.text: In a group of politicians one has equal status

indicators.note: In places the numeral inside the political group

parts.note: a political party is a group of politicians
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Within a political party each member claims equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality of status or value.

clue.text: Odd way to get fruit rounded off

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: rounded off means the round letter is removed

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: A peculiar way to get an orange peeled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounded off' means the round letter, O, is taken off the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd, unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: A regiment trained to shoot

indicators.note: trained suggests drilling into a new formation, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A regiment is trained in firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' looks like firing guns, but it is a plant sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to sprout, as a seed puts out a shoot.

clue.text: Doubter acting so oddly

indicators.note: oddly suggests these letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sceptic who behaves strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts whether the existence of God can be known.

clue.text: Rejected sweets but still put weight on

indicators.note: Rejected says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: desserts are sweets, the sweet course of a meal

explanation.surface: A dieter refused pudding but gained weight anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put weight on' looks like getting fatter, but it means emphasised.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to emphasise it, putting weight on it.

clue.text: Town where worker is in the money

indicators.note: is in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a wage is the money one earns
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A place where workers are well paid.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a market town in Oxfordshire, birthplace of Alfred the Great.

clue.text: Polecat making fellow blunder and in French!

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A man makes a mistake about a polecat in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferret is a domesticated form of the polecat.

clue.text: Relish resistance to cup holder

parts.note: a relish is a sauce or condiment
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A condiment opposes a cup holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is the small plate that holds a cup.

clue.text: Stop bread going off

indicators.note: going off suggests something spoiling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stop the bread going stale.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to prevent or prohibit, to stop someone doing something.

clue.text: Used to be made familiar

definitions.meaning: made familiar means habituated by experience

explanation.surface: Something once was made familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean habituated: being used to something and having been made familiar with it.

clue.text: Some fancy nickname for a pessimist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A name for a gloomy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for a pessimist' as the definition; 'for a' is a link, since only 'pessimist' can replace the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic expects the worst of people, much as a pessimist expects the worst outcome.

clue.text: It amplifies first message to old president

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker carries the first message to a former president.
explanation.definitionFit: A mike, short for microphone, picks up sound for amplification.

clue.text: Look at old leg trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbing, so the letters are stirred

explanation.surface: Examine an old leg injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone, usually lecherously.

clue.text: Find someone guilty of trick that brings six to court

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A verdict on a scam that brings six people to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To convict is to declare someone guilty in a court of law.

clue.text: Dogs' blankets

definitions.meaning: Afghan hounds are a long-haired breed of dog

explanation.surface: Blankets belonging to dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghan hounds are a breed of dog, and an afghan is also a knitted woollen blanket.

clue.text: Northern Ireland police with thousand to fire on kitbag

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force until 2001
to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: Ulster police with a thousand set out to dismiss a kitbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back, much like a kitbag.

clue.text: Justify having given food back at last

indicators.note: back says the word is turned round

parts.note: fed means given food
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Someone justifies feeding back at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend an action is to justify it by argument.
